title: Marcion
lead: Marcion, a Christian teacher from Pontus active in Rome in the mid second century, rejected the Old Testament and taught a distinction between the God of justice who made the world and a higher God of goodness revealed by Christ. The church rejected his teaching. Lake summarizes it this way in his notes to the Martyrdom of Polycarp.

sections.b: Irenaeus tells that when Marcion met Polycarp and said 'Do you know me?', Polycarp answered, 'I do know you, the first-born of Satan' (Against Heresies 3.3.4, ANF). Polycarp's letter uses the same phrase of those who twist the Lord's sayings (Polycarp to the Philippians 7:1); whether he already meant Marcion there is debated. The Moscow manuscript's ending of the Martyrdom of Polycarp repeats the story. The 'Marcion' who wrote up the Martyrdom (Martyrdom of Polycarp 20:1) is, Lake says, 'not of course to be identified with the famous heretic'.
